default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-238.title: Calm-week micro-break fade
E-238.hypothesis: When the last 5 sessions' average range is well below the 20-session average, the multi-day volatility regime is calm: dealers carry small inventories, no macro repositioning is under way and day traders cut their range expectations; a close beyond the recent high/low in such a week is a small push through quotes that liquidity providers lean back on, so fade it.

E-239.title: Previous-block midpoint rejection
E-239.hypothesis: The 50% level of the last completed 15/30/60-minute candle is where chart traders reading that timeframe split the candle into buyers' and sellers' halves and rest their re-entries; a bar that comes back to it from one side and closes back on that side shows those orders absorbing the pullback, so trade away from the midpoint (only when the block was wide enough to matter).

E-240.title: Stair-step break exhaustion fade
E-240.hypothesis: Several closes above the short-term high within half an hour with no opposite break is a stair-step of small breakout entries; each step adds late buyers with stops just below, and once the count is high the breakout pool is used up and their stops sit close, so fade the bar where the count is reached (mirror).

E-241.title: Wicked break-bar fade
E-241.hypothesis: A bar that closes above the recent high but leaves a large upper wick traded well beyond the level and was already sold back inside the same bar: sellers met the breakout at the new prices and the buyers who bought the bar's high are under water at once; fade the break (mirror for lows).

E-242.title: Multi-day overlap balance micro-break fade
E-242.hypothesis: When yesterday's range overlapped most of the day before's, the market has accepted the same price zone for two sessions (multi-day balance): swing traders sell its top and buy its bottom and nobody initiates; today's short-term breaks inside that regime lack an initiator and are faded.

E-243.title: Gap-filled day micro-break fade
E-243.hypothesis: Once an opening gap of meaningful size has been fully filled back to yesterday's close, local traders have reversed the overnight information and the session is run by responsive liquidity providers rather than by an overnight initiator; from then on short-term breaks are faded.

E-244.title: Outside-block micro-break fade
E-244.hypothesis: When the current clock block (30/60/120 minutes) has already traded beyond both the high and the low of the previous block, the stop pools on both sides of that candle are spent and the block is rotating two-way; a further short-term break inside such an outside block has no fresh stops to run and is faded.

E-245.title: VWAP-contested session micro-break fade
E-245.hypothesis: Many closes crossing the session VWAP over the last two hours mean neither side can hold price away from the day's average cost: value is contested and both camps trade responsively around it; a short-term break in that state is absorbed by the other camp, so fade it.

E-246.title: Clock-hour range quota fade
E-246.hypothesis: Short-term traders size targets on what a clock hour usually covers; when the current hour's range first reaches its 20-session typical range for that hour, the bar that set the new hour extreme is where their take-profits sit and the hour's directional flow is spent, so fade that bar.

E-247.title: Developing doji-day micro-break fade
E-247.hypothesis: After the first 90 minutes, a session whose price is back near its open despite a real range is drawing a doji on every daily chart: both sides tried and were rejected, and the day is being traded responsively; short-term breaks in that state lack an initiator and are faded.
